The Federal Government has inaugurated electricity infrastructure projects in Gombe State, including a new substation in Billiri and upgraded transformers at the Gombe Transmission Substation, increasing the latter’s upstream transmission capacity to 480MW. The projects were inaugurated on Thursday by the Minister of Power, Joseph Tegbe, who said they would strengthen electricity transmission and improve the capacity to meet growing demand in the state and neighbouring communities. At the Gombe Transmission Substation, Tegbe said the installation of an additional 300MVA, 330/132kV transformer had doubled the station’s upstream transmission capacity from 300MVA to 600MVA, equivalent to 480MW. He also said the replacement of an existing 30MVA, 132/33kV transformer with a 100MVA unit had increased the station’s downstream transformation capacity to 220MVA, equivalent to 176MW. “The growing electricity demand exceeded the capacity of the existing infrastructure, resulting in suppressed demand. To address this, an additional 300MVA, 330/132kV transformer has been installed, doubling the upstream transmission capacity to 600MVA, equivalent to 480MW. “Equally, the existing 30MVA transformer has been replaced with a 100MVA, 132/33kV transformer, increasing the downstream capacity to 220MVA, equivalent to 176MW,” the minister said. According to Tegbe, the upgrades are expected to provide additional capacity for electricity consumers and accommodate more than 70,000 additional households. The minister said the projects reflected President Bola Tinubu’s commitment to strengthening the national grid and addressing electricity supply challenges. Funded by the World Bank and executed by Chris Ejik International Limited, the facility has six outgoing 33kV feeders and is connected to the existing Gombe-Savannah-Yola transmission line. Tegbe said the substation would support agricultural activities, businesses and growing settlements in the area. “The commercial exchanges, agricultural activities, small enterprises and growing settlements within this axis require electricity that is both accessible and dependable,” he said. He added that the investment would extend the transmission network and give communities access to infrastructure needed to support economic activities. The minister urged residents to protect the facilities against vandalism, warning that attacks on electricity infrastructure could disrupt businesses and household livelihoods. Earlier, the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Transmission Company of Nigeria, Sule Ahmed Abdulaziz, said the Billiri substation would strengthen the interface between transmission and distribution networks. Abdulaziz also urged the distribution company to increase its offtake of available electricity to ensure that residents and businesses benefit from the investment. At the Gombe Transmission Substation, he said the reinforcement project was awarded to ISIN Electromechanical Industries Limited in June 2021 and completed in June 2026. He explained that the contractor handled the design, manufacture, supply, testing, installation and commissioning of the transformers, as well as supporting structures and auxiliary equipment. Abdulaziz said replacing transformers at an operational transmission station was technically demanding because electricity supply had to be maintained while the old equipment was removed and the new units installed. Representing Governor Muhammadu Yahaya, the Commissioner for Energy Resources, Sanusi Ahmad, said the projects would strengthen the state’s electricity infrastructure and support economic expansion. He said the state government had earlier commissioned two additional 33kV outgoing feeders in December 2023. Ahmad also said the state was taking advantage of the Electricity Act 2023 through the implementation of the Gombe State Electricity Law 2025 and the establishment of the Gombe State Electricity Regulatory Commission. “Our administration will continue to engage relevant Federal Government institutions, electricity market operators, private investors and development partners to explore opportunities that will further strengthen electricity supply across Gombe State,” he said. The Mai Tangle, Danladi Sanusi, also commended the investment, describing the Billiri substation as a source of economic opportunity for the area. He said improved electricity supply could stimulate businesses, attract investors, create jobs and improve healthcare and education. The traditional ruler, however, urged the authorities to ensure proper maintenance and effective utilisation of the facilities to guarantee lasting benefits. Chima Azubuike
